question: A 52-year-old Caucasian male presents to your office with an 8 mm dark lesion on his back. The lesion, as seen below, has irregular borders and marked internal color variation. Upon excisional biopsy, the presence of which of the following would best estimate the risk of metastasis in this patient’s lesion:?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Irregular borders and marked internal color variation" -> "suspicion of melanoma" -> "excisional biopsy performed" -> "histopathological examination" -> "identification of cellular atypia" -> "increased risk of metastasis" -> 80% CHAIN: "Excisional biopsy" -> "identification of vertical tumor growth" -> "increased risk of metastasis" -> 75% CHAIN: "Presence of palisading nuclei" -> "suggestive of basal cell carcinoma" -> "lower risk of metastasis" -> 70% CHAIN: "Increased production of melanosomes" -> "suggestive of melanoma" -> "increased risk of metastasis" -> 80%
analysis: The presence of vertical tumor growth is a key feature associated with increased risk of metastasis in melanoma. This indicates invasion of tumor cells into deeper layers of the skin, which is a concerning sign for potential spread to other parts of the body.
